text: The mayor of this village is afraid of the same man everyone else is afraid of, which is what a local strongman amounts to in practice. A death brings an investigator, Garcia Mata, out to ask questions, and he finds a town that has already decided what it can afford to say. Mexican critics later placed the film among the hundred best the country has made, and the reason sits in its arithmetic rather than its plot: authority without leverage, a population with everything to lose, ninety minutes of pressure applied to both. Gavaldón does not treat the crime as a puzzle. The facts are local knowledge. What the film watches is the cost of saying them out loud, which is a slower kind of suspense, and which turns an ordinary answer to an ordinary question into an act.

A woman named Ilona has disappeared, and the search for her runs through boardrooms and laboratories rather than alleys, none of it photographed, all of it drawn. Karas goes looking, and the worlds he has to enter are corporate espionage, organized crime and genetic research, which is to say three different ways of owning a person. The premise puts a price on the body and then makes someone negotiate it. Animation commits the film to a city with no found detail: every wet street and glass front is a decision, and a French feature spending 105 minutes on that labour is arguing that most of a thriller is weather and surface. It took the Cristal for a feature at Annecy. The plot underneath is the oldest one there is, a man asking who took her, carried by images that had to be made from nothing.

Be like Dad, Keep Mum: the slogan is on the wall behind the actors, and the picture is built to prove the wall right. Britain, 1943 - the argument is that a careless remark in a pub can end on a German desk, and Dickinson gives it a mechanism rather than a moral, information leaking in small forgivable increments while the audience is placed where it can watch the leak travel. None of the plotting is decorative. Being told a thing is dangerous does less work than being shown the route it takes, which is why the case is assembled in stages instead of announced. That is the discipline of it: 102 minutes that treat gossip as a supply chain. The National Board of Review named it one of the ten best films of its year, an unusual afterlife for a picture whose first job was instruction.

The event has already happened; the day is spent making it happen again, correctly, for a camera. A prosecutor, a policeman and a teacher take two students back to the restaurant where they got drunk and fought, so the brawl can be re-staged and filmed as a warning to others. Romania, 1968: the method - reconstruct, record, instruct - is handed the whole running time and left to demonstrate itself. Comedy sits beside drama in the genre line and both are earned, because official patience is funny, and it stops being funny at a rate nobody in the frame controls. Romanian critics later voted the film into their all-time top ten. What the two boys did takes a minute to perform. What is being done to them takes all day.

He sells the company he built and books the long-promised passage to Europe, and somewhere on the way it becomes clear that his wife wants a different trip. The National Film Registry keeps it and TIME later put it on a list of a hundred for all time, which is considerable institutional weight for a film in which nothing occurs but two people being honest at different speeds. Retirement is the engine. A man who ran a factory suddenly has time, and time turns out to be what the marriage was arranged to avoid. Wyler stages the disagreement as manners - which hotel, which company, what an evening is for - so the damage arrives in ordinary rooms and ordinary voices, unmistakable long before anyone in the film is willing to name it.

The house sits between a Palestinian village and an Israeli settlement, which makes it a position before it is a home. The army occupies it; Mohammed, his wife and their five children stay. His refusal to leave is the entire plot, and it is dramatized as household logistics rather than argument - where seven people may stand, when they may move, how a family eats and sleeps under rules it did not write and cannot appeal. Ninety minutes is the right length, because the situation does not develop so much as persist. The production is Italian, the language is Arabic, and it left with a Golden Leopard. What it understands is that occupation at this scale is not made of gunfire but of permission, asked for, granted or refused, several times a day.

A husband decides that jealousy might do the work desire no longer will, and arranges for his daughter's lover to spend time with his wife. Everyone in the house is being used, including the man doing the using. Awards followed it out of Japan - a Jury Prize, a Golden Globe for a film not in English, the Samuel Goldwyn International Award - a curious reception for a picture whose real subject is a scheme running quietly beneath the family meals. Ichikawa is less interested in appetite than in administration: who is told what, who is permitted to notice, how long a household can hold a shape it knows to be false. 107 minutes, and the temperature never rises into farce or falls into confession. The husband's calculation is that a body can be argued into wanting. The film watches the argument being made.

Three people who barely meet share one summer in northern Scania: a seasonal worker new to Sweden, a young man home with a broken heart, a girl loose in her first vacation. Seventy-six minutes assembled from fragments, some plain and a few tipping toward the magical, is a structure that holds only if the landscape does the joining. Here it does. Faces give way to fields and weather, and the three lives thin out until they are hard to lift free of the place they happen in. The unit of attention is the fragment rather than the scene: a job, an errand, an afternoon that leads nowhere in particular. The DOX:AWARD went to it. What is at stake is small and not negotiable - work that lasts exactly as long as a crop lasts, a homecoming that ends when the holiday does, a summer a child gets once.
